latent_mechanisms.display_name: Transformed aggressive B-cell clone emerging from CLL/SLL
latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Expansion of a large-cell lymphoma clone arising in the context of chronic lymphocytic leukemia or small lymphocytic lymphoma. This is the central Richter transformation mechanism and is distinct from baseline indolent CLL burden.

Rapid lymphoma growth with high Ki-67, MYC activation, TP53 disruption, complex karyotype, or double-hit biology in subsets. Drives abrupt clinical change, high FDG avidity, LDH release, bulky mass growth, and tumor lysis pressure.

latent_mechanisms.display_name: Rapid lymphoma cell turnover and LDH release
latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Cell death and membrane turnover from fast-growing transformed lymphoma releases LDH and intracellular metabolites. LDH elevation is a common presentation clue and adverse prognostic signal.

latent_mechanisms.display_name: Rapid nodal and mass-forming lymphoma expansion
latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Accelerated growth within one or more lymph node regions, often discordant with otherwise stable CLL adenopathy. Produces rapidly enlarging nodes, bulky masses, pain, ureteric compression, and biopsy targets.

Large-cell Richter transformation involving liver, lung, bone marrow, gastrointestinal tract, kidney/adrenal, skin, or other organs. It can dominate the presentation even when nodal disease is absent or unchanged.

Parenchymal or leptomeningeal large-cell lymphoma infiltration in the setting of CLL/SLL transformation. Rare but high-risk; may present with focal neurologic deficits, headache, CSF abnormalities, or a mass lesion.
IL-6, TNF, IL-1, and tumor microenvironment cytokine activity causing fever, night sweats, weight loss, fatigue, low albumin, anemia of inflammation, and occasional HLH-like pressure.

Underlying CLL/SLL biology creates immune dysfunction, hypogammaglobulinemia, impaired T-cell surveillance, and a permissive background for transformation and infection complications. It is not the same as the transformed large-cell clone.

latent_mechanisms.display_name: Marrow replacement by CLL and/or transformed lymphoma
latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Bone marrow involvement by baseline CLL, transformed large-cell lymphoma, or both. Causes anemia, thrombocytopenia, neutropenia, and treatment intolerance; interpretation requires avoiding double counting with baseline CLL cytopenias.
High tumor burden and high proliferation create spontaneous or treatment-triggered tumor lysis risk with urate, phosphate, potassium release and kidney injury hazard.

Cytotoxic chemoimmunotherapy causes neutropenia, anemia, thrombocytopenia, febrile neutropenia, and secondary infection risk. This is a treatment-state mechanism rather than untreated Richter biology.

A subset of aggressive lymphoma presentations can trigger HLH/MAS physiology through cytokine amplification. HLH/MAS remains a complication/event axis, not a mimic mechanism defining Richter transformation.

mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: Richter transformation emerges from a CLL/SLL background; CLL immune dysregulation and clonal evolution create the permissive substrate.
Large-cell transformation is clinically recognized through aggressive growth kinetics rather than indolent CLL tempo.
High proliferation produces high cell turnover and LDH release.
Most cases present with new or rapidly enlarging nodal disease.
Transformed lymphoma can spread to extranodal organs and may be the dominant diagnostic clue.

mechanism_edges.conditionality: Rare CNS-predominant or CNS-relapsed Richter presentations.
mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: CNS disease is an extranodal sanctuary-site expression of transformed lymphoma.
Tumor burden and microenvironment cytokines produce B symptoms and acute phase response.

mechanism_edges.conditionality: Marrow involvement by CLL, transformed lymphoma, or both.
mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: Marrow disease is an extranodal compartment that drives cytopenias and treatment tolerance.
Bulky high-grade lymphoma has spontaneous and treatment-triggered tumor lysis risk.

mechanism_edges.conditionality: EBV-positive, advanced, or highly inflammatory lymphoma contexts.
mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: Cytokine-rich aggressive lymphoma can trigger HLH/MAS physiology.
Nodal transformation produces new or discordantly enlarging adenopathy.
Clinical or radiographic lymphadenopathy severity tracks nodal transformed disease.
Abrupt growth over weeks is a key clinical trigger for RT evaluation.
Mass-forming growth reflects transformed nodal burden.
Largest mass dimension captures bulky transformed nodal disease.
Bulky pelvic nodal masses can produce focal pain.
Extranodal transformed disease creates measurable non-nodal lesions.
Extent of non-nodal organ involvement reflects extranodal transformation burden.
Liver lesions can be the biopsy target in extranodal RT.
Transformed lymphoma can form FDG-avid pulmonary nodules.
CNS infiltration defines neurologic Richter involvement.
Parenchymal Richter lymphoma can appear as a measurable enhancing brain mass.
Focal CNS lesions or leptomeningeal disease produce neurologic deficits.
CNS mass effect, meningeal irritation, or CSF disease may produce headache.
LDH rises with high-grade lymphoma turnover and tumor burden.
LDH/ULN is robust across laboratories and often used in RT suspicion.
High-grade transformation is FDG-avid; PET identifies the highest-yield biopsy site.
SUVmax is a quantitative PET marker used to select biopsy targets in suspected RT.
Tumor cytokines cause fever independent of infection.
Drenching sweats are a common lymphoma B symptom.
Cachexia and appetite loss can develop over weeks to months.
Inflammation, anemia, and tumor burden drive fatigue.
IL-6 acute-phase response may elevate CRP even without infection.
Albumin is suppressed as a negative acute-phase reactant and by cancer cachexia.
Marrow infiltration and inflammation can produce anemia.
Marrow replacement and hypersplenism may reduce platelets.
Baseline CLL can produce lymphocytosis that should not be interpreted as transformed lymphoma burden by itself.
Liver involvement or reticuloendothelial expansion can cause hepatomegaly.

mechanism_edges.conditionality: Splenic involvement or baseline CLL reticuloendothelial disease.
mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: Splenomegaly may reflect CLL, transformed lymphoma, or both.
High tumor burden and cytoreduction can precipitate clinical TLS.
Chemoimmunotherapy causes neutropenic fever risk during count nadir.
Neutropenia, steroids, anti-CD20 therapy, and CLL immune dysfunction increase infections.
Lymphoma-associated macrophage activation pressure raises HLH/MAS event risk.
Untreated or refractory Richter transformation has high short-term mortality.

axes.shape_free_text: Presence of known or concurrently diagnosed CLL/SLL. This distinguishes Richter transformation from de novo DLBCL but should not by itself prove transformation.
Indolent CLL blood/marrow burden. It explains lymphocytosis and baseline adenopathy but should not double count transformed large-cell tumor burden.
Can be high from CLL and may be normal during Richter transformation. Do not require lymphocytosis for RT.
Often reflects background CLL lymphocytosis, infection, steroids, or marrow failure rather than transformed mass itself.
Any clinically or radiographically pathologic lymph node enlargement. Parent finding for nodal mass burden satellites.
Overall severity of nodal enlargement after parent pathologic lymphadenopathy is present.
Weeks-scale growth or discordant node enlargement compared with stable baseline CLL nodes.
Mass-forming nodal disease such as pelvic, retroperitoneal, mediastinal, cervical, or abdominal nodal conglomerate.
Direct image measurement of the largest nodal mass or nodal conglomerate.
Any non-nodal organ lesion attributable to lymphoma burden after clinical/imaging evaluation.
Overall extent of extranodal RT lesions across organs.
Liver lesions or hepatic infiltration by transformed lymphoma.
Pulmonary nodular lesion burden; in cases this should be interpreted alongside infection and second cancer exclusions.
Clinical/imaging activity of CNS lymphoma involvement. CSF cytology or tissue proof belongs in confirmatory_findings.
Largest diameter of a CNS mass lesion on MRI or CT.
Focal weakness, speech disturbance, cranial neuropathy, seizure, or encephalopathy severity.
Headache, especially in CNS involvement; nonspecific and shared with infection, vascular, and inflammatory mimics.
Fever as a lymphoma B symptom. Infection evidence must be separately represented rather than inferred away.
Drenching night sweats or similar constitutional sweating.
Unintentional weight loss when exact percent or baseline weight is unavailable.
Fatigue from lymphoma cytokines, anemia, or treatment.
Focal pelvic pain from pelvic nodal mass, ureteric obstruction, bone involvement, or other local mass effect.
Liver enlargement from infiltration or reticuloendothelial disease.
Spleen enlargement from baseline CLL/SLL, transformed lymphoma, or both.
Anemia may arise from marrow infiltration, inflammation, autoimmune hemolysis, bleeding, or treatment.
Thrombocytopenia may reflect marrow disease, hypersplenism, autoimmune cytopenia, or treatment.
Neutropenia can be baseline marrow failure or treatment-induced; neutrophilia can reflect infection or steroids.
LDH elevation supports high-grade lymphoma turnover but can be normal in localized or CNS-predominant cases.
Scaled LDH permits comparison across laboratory reference ranges.
Can rise from lymphoma cytokines or infection; do not use alone to decide between RT and infection.
Negative acute-phase reactant and nutritional/cachexia marker.
Tumor burden and renal function marker in CLL/lymphoma; not specific for RT.
Renal function context for TLS, obstruction, cisplatin, methotrexate, and supportive care.

axes.display_name: High FDG uptake activity on PET/CT
axes.shape_free_text: Markedly FDG-avid focus or lesion cluster used to guide biopsy. Infection and second cancer can mimic this, so tissue proof remains confirmatory.

axes.display_name: PET/CT SUVmax in suspected Richter lesion
axes.shape_free_text: Quantitative SUVmax when reported. Missing exact SUV should not block using qualitative PET burden axes.
Marrow involvement by CLL or transformed lymphoma; marrow biopsy proof should be stored as confirmatory context in case files.
Evidence for bacterial, viral, fungal, or opportunistic infection that can mimic RT. It is an observed context axis, not a Richter latent mechanism.
Biopsy/IHC evidence of large B-cell transformation. Case files should store this under confirmatory_findings, not ordinary observations.
Pathology context distinguishing Hodgkin transformation/Richter syndrome from DLBCL-type RT; not an ordinary presentation observation.
IGH/IGK or genomic evidence that transformed lymphoma is clonally related to CLL. Store as confirmatory context.
MYC with BCL2 or BCL6 rearrangement in transformed lymphoma; a pathology/cytogenetics context and treatment-effect modifier.
Anti-CD20 treatment context from flow/IHC. Confirmation belongs outside ordinary presentation observations.
Cardiac function and frailty context for anthracycline-containing chemoimmunotherapy.
Fitness, organ function, donor/collection feasibility, and remission state context for CAR-T or transplant strategies.
Prior ibrutinib, acalabrutinib, zanubrutinib, or pirtobrutinib exposure; modifies likelihood of BTK-pathway response.
Prior BCL2 inhibitor exposure; modifies venetoclax-based cytoreduction response and TLS planning.
Baseline cytopenias that limit dose intensity or increase infection/bleeding complications.
HBsAg or anti-HBc context relevant to anti-CD20 therapy.
Ureteric compression or hydronephrosis risk from pelvic/retroperitoneal mass.

axes.display_name: CNS progression hazard in Richter transformation
axes.shape_free_text: Risk of neurologic progression, recurrent CNS mass, leptomeningeal progression, or neurologic death.

axes.display_name: Tumor lysis syndrome hazard in Richter transformation
axes.shape_free_text: TLS event hazard from bulky high-turnover disease and cytoreductive therapy.

axes.display_name: Febrile neutropenia hazard in Richter transformation
axes.shape_free_text: Neutropenic fever risk during chemoimmunotherapy or cellular therapy-associated cytopenias.
Infection hazard from CLL immune dysfunction, cytotoxic therapy, steroids, anti-CD20, CAR-T, or transplant.
Macrophage activation/HLH event hazard. It distinguishes a complication chain from baseline lymphoma fever.
Lifespan outcome hazard for Richter transformation; integrates transformed burden, refractory disease, CNS disease, TLS, HLH/MAS, infection, and treatment toxicity.

axis_couplings.conditionality: Pelvic or retroperitoneal mass adjacent to ureter or renal hilum.
axis_couplings.clinical_rationale: Bulky pelvic nodal disease can compress ureters and cause hydronephrosis or kidney injury.
Untreated obstruction worsens kidney function, limits methotrexate/cisplatin options, and increases complications.
Active CNS involvement raises risk of neurologic progression and early death.
Progressive CNS Richter disease is associated with rapid neurologic decline.
TLS can cause acute kidney injury with creatinine rise.
Severe TLS can cause kidney failure, arrhythmia, ICU admission, and death.
Febrile neutropenia is a pathway to severe bacterial or fungal infection.
Infection and sepsis are major treatment-course mortality drivers in CLL/RT.
Lymphoma-associated HLH/MAS can rapidly increase organ failure and death risk.
Both LDH and PET avidity reflect aggressive tumor metabolism, but neither causes the other.
B symptoms cluster through shared cytokine drive.
Multilineage cytopenias often move together when marrow reserve is impaired.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Anti-CD20 effect depends on CD20 expression.
Low cardiac or frailty fitness limits anthracycline delivery.
Double-hit biology often requires deeper cytoreduction and has higher relapse risk.

side_effects.interpretation: Neutropenia, steroid exposure, and anti-CD20 B-cell depletion.
Early cytoreduction of bulky high-turnover disease.

treatments.context_specific_role: Anthracycline-based chemoimmunotherapy option for CD20-positive DLBCL-type Richter transformation when fitness permits.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: High-grade/double-hit biology can justify deeper dose-adjusted cytoreduction in fit patients.
Baseline marrow failure limits dose adjustment and increases infection risk.

treatments.context_specific_role: More intensive chemoimmunotherapy candidate for fit patients with high-grade proliferative biology.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Cisplatin/cytarabine-containing salvage is constrained by kidney function.
Salvage benefit is greater when it can bridge to cellular therapy or transplant.
Prior BCL2 inhibitor resistance can reduce response.
Venetoclax requires ramp-up and TLS prophylaxis in bulky/high-turnover disease.

side_effects.interpretation: Venetoclax-associated neutropenia when combined with chemotherapy or antibodies.

treatments.context_specific_role: Targeted combination option, often studied with chemoimmunotherapy or anti-CD20 therapy; requires TLS-aware implementation.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Prior BTK inhibitor progression suggests pathway resistance.
BTK inhibitors may control concurrent CLL component even if large-cell RT response is incomplete.

side_effects.interpretation: Infection risk in heavily pretreated CLL/RT context.

treatments.context_specific_role: Targeted component for CLL control, selected RT subsets, or post-induction maintenance strategies.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Frailty, uncontrolled infection, organ failure, or inability to bridge reduces feasibility.
High tumor burden increases cytokine-release and cytopenia complications.

side_effects.interpretation: B-cell aplasia, cytopenias, and post-cellular therapy immune suppression.
Neurotoxicity may clinically overlap CNS disease; it is not tumor progression.

treatments.context_specific_role: Cellular immunotherapy option for relapsed/refractory DLBCL-type RT when disease can be bridged and patient fitness allows.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Requires remission or responsive disease, donor/fitness, and organ reserve.
Uncontrolled infection or profound immune compromise increases non-relapse mortality.

side_effects.interpretation: Conditioning, GVHD prophylaxis, and immune reconstitution.

treatments.context_specific_role: Potential consolidation for selected fit patients with responsive disease; toxicity and timing dominate feasibility.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Direct effect is expected when CNS disease is present or high-risk prophylaxis is selected.
High-dose methotrexate clearance depends on renal function.

treatments.context_specific_role: CNS-directed treatment or prophylaxis context; must be paired with systemic disease control when systemic RT exists.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Radiation can rapidly palliate focal mass pain.
CNS radiation targets local neurologic mass effect rather than systemic disease.

treatments.context_specific_role: Local symptom control, bulky lesion palliation, or selected CNS/local consolidation context.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Highest benefit when TLS hazard is high.
Renal impairment increases TLS consequence and need for prophylaxis.

side_effects.interpretation: Volume or urate management failure if prophylaxis insufficient.

treatments.context_specific_role: TLS prevention and mitigation during cytoreductive therapy.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Benefit is greatest when neutropenic fever risk is high.

treatments.context_specific_role: Myeloid support during intensive chemoimmunotherapy or prolonged cytopenia.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Anti-CD20 therapy strongly increases HBV reactivation risk.
Antiviral, PJP, and antibacterial/fungal prophylaxis are context-dependent on immune deficit.

side_effects.interpretation: Some antimicrobial prophylaxis can contribute to cytopenia.

treatments.context_specific_role: Prevention of HBV reactivation, PJP, HSV/VZV, bacterial, or fungal infection according to immune and regimen context.

CLL_or_SLL_present.trajectory_modulation: Required disease context for Richter transformation; by itself it explains lymphocytosis and baseline adenopathy, not transformed large-cell kinetics.

axis_response_modulation.clinical_rationale: Schema-normalized from compact risk modulation without changing the underlying clinical direction.
Schema-normalized from compact risk modulation without changing the underlying clinical direction.

high_risk_BCR_context.trajectory_modulation: Higher transformation risk and more aggressive CLL biology.

TP53_aberrant.trajectory_modulation: Greater refractory risk and mortality hazard under chemoimmunotherapy.

axis_response_modulation.clinical_rationale: Schema-normalized from compact risk modulation without changing the underlying clinical direction.

NOTCH1_mutated.trajectory_modulation: Associated with higher RT risk and aggressive clonal evolution.

complex_or_double_hit.trajectory_modulation: Amplifies aggressive proliferation, LDH release, PET avidity, and refractory risk.

axis_response_modulation.clinical_rationale: Schema-normalized from compact risk modulation without changing the underlying clinical direction.
Schema-normalized from compact risk modulation without changing the underlying clinical direction.

multiple_prior_lines_or_purine_analog_ex.trajectory_modulation: Often less fit and more immunosuppressed; higher infection and refractory risk.

axis_response_modulation.clinical_rationale: Schema-normalized from compact risk modulation without changing the underlying clinical direction.

novel_agent_refractory.trajectory_modulation: May indicate selected aggressive resistant clones and weaker targeted-agent reuse.

age_over_75_or_low_fitness.trajectory_modulation: Does not define RT but changes treatment tolerance, infection hazard, and transplant/CAR-T feasibility.

axis_response_modulation.clinical_rationale: Schema-normalized from compact risk modulation without changing the underlying clinical direction.
Schema-normalized from compact risk modulation without changing the underlying clinical direction.

EBV_or_iatrogenic_immunosuppression.trajectory_modulation: Can favor Hodgkin-pattern transformation or EBV-driven large-cell biology; pathology context decides subtype.

clonal_relatedness_present.trajectory_modulation: Confirms biology closer to true transformed CLL and generally worse behavior than clonally unrelated de novo DLBCL in a patient with CLL.

axis_response_modulation.clinical_rationale: Schema-normalized from compact risk modulation without changing the underlying clinical direction.

supportive_care: PET/CT to map metabolic heterogeneity and choose the most FDG-avid, clinically accessible biopsy target.
Core or excisional biopsy of the suspicious lesion for morphology, IHC, flow cytometry, Ki-67, EBER, and FISH/cytogenetics; store these as confirmatory evidence in cases.
Separate baseline CLL burden from transformed lymphoma burden to avoid double counting lymphocytosis and old stable adenopathy.
Pathology review to distinguish DLBCL-type RT, Hodgkin-pattern transformation, accelerated CLL, de novo DLBCL in a patient with CLL, infection, and second primary malignancy.
Clonal relationship testing when available because clonally unrelated disease behaves more like de novo lymphoma.
Baseline staging with PET/CT, CT/MRI for organ-specific symptoms, bone marrow assessment when cytopenias are unexplained, and CNS evaluation when neurologic symptoms or high-risk features exist.
Baseline CBC differential, LDH with upper normal reference, CMP including creatinine and liver tests, uric acid/phosphate/potassium/calcium for TLS planning, beta-2 microglobulin when available.
Infection evaluation before attributing fever or FDG-avid lesions to RT, especially in immunosuppressed CLL patients.
Pre-treatment cardiac evaluation before anthracycline; renal function review before platinum, cytarabine, or high-dose methotrexate.
HBV, HCV, HIV testing and HBV prophylaxis/monitoring for anti-CD20-containing therapy.
TLS prophylaxis and monitoring before cytoreductive therapy in bulky, high-LDH, renal-impaired, or venetoclax-exposed settings.
Growth factor, antimicrobial prophylaxis, transfusion support, and rapid febrile neutropenia pathways during intensive therapy.
CNS-directed imaging/CSF evaluation and treatment planning when headache, focal deficit, brain lesion, or CSF abnormalities are present.
Early referral for cellular therapy or transplant assessment when disease is responsive and patient fitness allows.
Palliative care and local radiation integration for pain, neurologic compromise, obstruction, or refractory disease while systemic options are assessed.
